README: This file drives the firmware dropdown in the web flasher.
A build gets its binary in one of two ways: a pinned url, or a release block.
A build with neither shows up greyed out and cannot be flashed, which is deliberate:
nothing is offered that cannot actually be downloaded.
PINNED URL (url / offset / sha256)
url    : a direct link to a MERGED firmware image (bootloader + partitions + app
in one file). A GitHub release asset works, as long as it is a single
merged .bin. Build one with: esptool.py --chip esp32 merge_bin -o merged.bin
--flash_mode dio --flash_size 4MB 0x1000 bootloader.bin 0x8000 partitions.bin
0x10000 firmware.bin
offset : where that image starts. A merged image is 0. A bare app image is usually
65536 (0x10000). A typo here is refused rather than treated as 0, because
writing an app image over the bootloader bricks the board.
sha256 : optional but strongly recommended. The SHA-256 of the exact file at url.
When present the browser verifies the download before writing anything, so
a swapped or tampered release asset is refused. Get it with:
sha256sum merged.bin        (Linux/macOS)
certutil -hashfile merged.bin SHA256   (Windows)
Without it the flasher warns in its console that the download is unverified.
RELEASE BLOCK (release)
Pulls the project's own latest GitHub release at flash time, so the site does not go
stale every time upstream ships. The trade is that the file is whatever upstream just
published, so it CANNOT be checksummed against anything here, and the flasher says so
in its console before every such write. Fields:
repo    : owner/repo, e.g. pr3y/Bruce. Anything else is refused.
include : substrings that must ALL appear in the asset filename, case-insensitive.
exclude : substrings that must appear in NONE of them. Use this to drop the separate
bootloader and partition files that some projects also attach.
offset  : where the chosen asset gets written. Same rules as offset above.
note    : optional, shown under the build dropdown. Use it for anything the person
has to know before writing, such as an image being app-only.
These are substring filters, not regexes, on purpose. Upstream names assets per BOARD,
not per chip family, so the matching files are listed and the person picks their board.
If a filter matches nothing, the flasher lists every .bin in the release instead and
says the filter has gone stale, so a rename upstream degrades rather than breaks.
Two things to check when you add a URL or a repo:
1. The host must send CORS headers. GitHub release assets do. If a download fails
with a CORS error, put the .bin in this repo under assets/firmware/ and use a
relative path like assets/firmware/bruce-esp32.bin instead.
2. Any external host must be listed in connect-src in the CSP, both in the meta tag
in index.html and in _headers. api.github.com, github.com and the two
githubusercontent asset hosts are already there.
The include/exclude filters below were written from each project's documented naming
and have NOT been checked against a live release. Open the flasher once and look at
the build dropdown: if it says the filter went stale, tighten these to the real names.

release.note: Marauder publishes app-only images, written at 0x10000. That assumes the board already carries the Marauder bootloader. On a blank board, use the official installer linked under Order Links first.
